title: API 580 Training in Mobile, AL: RBI Exam Prep Online
description: API 580 risk based inspection exam prep for Mobile planners, engineers and inspectors at refineries and chemical plants: self-paced, with instructor Q&A.
h1: API 580 Training in Mobile, Alabama: Risk Based Inspection Exam Prep for Refinery and Chemical Corridor RBI Programmes
html:
API 580 exam prep for RBI teams in and around Mobile

Risk-based inspection is how a site with thousands of pieces of fixed equipment decides where its inspection effort goes. Around Mobile that question is asked at a hydroprocessing refinery at Saraland, at a large refinery just over the state line in Pascagoula, and across a chemical corridor where one complex alone runs 28 production plants. API 580, the Risk Based Inspection certification, tests whether you understand the principles behind those decisions as API RP 580 sets them out. This page is for the inspection planners, mechanical integrity engineers, corrosion specialists and senior inspectors who sit on RBI teams in the Mobile area.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Mobile. The API 580 course is self-paced and online, and an instructor answers your questions as you study, which suits engineers whose working week is already full of meetings and data reviews. API determines eligibility, administers the closed-book examination and certifies those who pass; the course is preparation, it grants no certificate, and Atlantis is not an API-approved training provider.

Who sits API 580 on the Alabama and Mississippi coast

Three groups make up most candidates. The first is inspectors who already hold API 510, API 570 or API 653 and want the risk vocabulary their RBI software and procedures use; a current certification in any of those three qualifies them automatically. The second is reliability and mechanical integrity engineers, often chemical or mechanical graduates, who run damage mechanism reviews and RBI workshops without holding an inspector certification. The third is inspection planners and data coordinators who turn RBI output into work orders and need to understand what the numbers mean before they schedule against them.

For candidates without one of the inspector certifications, API asks for education plus petrochemical industry experience gained in the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree, three with a high school diploma and five or more without formal education. A chemical engineering graduate of the University of South Alabama who spends a year on a refinery or chemical plant integrity team is therefore eligible sooner than most technicians, though API checks the experience described on the application.

The mechanical integrity rules an RBI programme serves

Alabama's Boiler and Pressure Vessel Safety Act exempts pressure vessels associated with oil and gas operations, from refining to storage, and vessels that form part of a manufacturing process, so on this corridor inspection planning is driven by federal process safety rules and the owner's chosen codes rather than a state inspection cycle. Under EPA's risk management programme rule, 40 CFR 68.73 requires a Program 3 process to maintain the mechanical integrity of pressure vessels and storage tanks, piping systems and valves, relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown systems, controls and pumps. Inspection and testing must follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, at a frequency consistent with manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practice, and more often if operating experience shows it is needed. Each inspection is documented with the date, the inspector's name, the equipment identifier, a description of the inspection and the results. OSHA's process safety management standard carries a parallel mechanical integrity element for the same equipment.

RBI does not replace those obligations. It is one recognised way of deciding what "a frequency consistent with good engineering practice" means for each item, and it is accepted because the inspection codes themselves allow it: API 510 and API 570 both permit intervals to be set from an RBI assessment, subject to the conditions each code attaches. An API 580 candidate should be able to explain that chain, from regulation to code to RBI assessment to inspection plan, in plain language, because that is what an auditor asks the RBI team.

What the current Body of Knowledge examines

The 2026 Body of Knowledge for API 580 is built on one publication: API RP 580, Elements of a Risk-Based Inspection Program, fourth edition, with its first addendum. It divides the examination into ten categories: terms, definitions and acronyms; risk assessment; the RBI programme; roles, responsibilities, training and qualifications; data collection; damage mechanisms; probability of failure; consequence of failure; risk management; and RBI documentation. The exam has 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 of them scored, in 3.25 hours, and no references are allowed.

CategoryWhat to be able to do without the book
Risk assessmentExplain qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches and when each is fit for purpose
Data collectionSay which design, construction, process, inspection and maintenance data an assessment needs and what to do when it is missing
Damage mechanismsLink a mechanism to its failure mode and to the inspection that can detect it
Probability and consequenceDescribe what drives each, including inspection effectiveness and the release, flammable, toxic and environmental outcomes
Risk managementDistinguish reducing uncertainty through inspection from reducing risk by other mitigation
DocumentationList what must be recorded so a later team can reproduce and update the assessment

RP 581, the quantitative method many software packages implement, is not listed in the 2026 Body of Knowledge, so the exam tests concepts rather than RP 581 equations.

Local study cases: changes of service and reassessment

RP 580 expects an RBI assessment to be revisited when something that drove it changes. Public information about Mobile-area plants supplies good examples to think through while you study, without needing any company's internal data.

  • A hydrocracker that changed feed twice. Vertex converted the Saraland hydrocracker to renewable diesel in 2023 and returned it to crude-derived feeds the following year. Each change alters the process fluid, the water and acid content, and the hydrogen sulfide and hydrogen conditions, so the damage mechanisms, the probability of failure and possibly the consequence model all need fresh review. Ask yourself which data a team would need before and after such a change, and how management of change connects to the RBI reassessment.
  • A new unit at the design stage. Vertex has approved a project to produce Group III base oils from its hydrocracker's vacuum gas oil, with a high-pressure lubricants hydrotreating unit procured and production planned for 2029. Risk thinking applied before start-up is cheap, because material selection, corrosion allowance and inspection access can still be changed on paper.
  • Production lines being shut down. BASF has said several lines at McIntosh will stop by spring 2027 while the site continues at a smaller footprint. Equipment that is idled, mothballed or isolated from a live process still needs a decision: removed from the assessment, assessed for its layup condition, or kept in the programme for a restart.

Consequence of failure around a bay

Consequence is where the Mobile corridor differs most from an inland refinery town. A chlor-alkali plant at McIntosh makes chlorine, so toxic release dominates the consequence picture for parts of that site in a way flammable release does not. The Pascagoula refinery, at 356,440 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation in EIA's survey for the start of 2026, has hydrocarbon inventories large enough that flammable consequence and business interruption carry heavy weight. Facilities on the river and the bay add environmental consequence for releases that reach water. An API 580 candidate does not need to calculate any of these on the exam, but should be able to say which consequence categories RP 580 recognises, why consequence is assessed separately from probability, and why the same corrosion rate can sit in very different risk positions at two sites.

A closed-book drill: which action lowers which part of the risk?

RP 580 draws a line that the exam returns to often: inspection reduces risk by reducing uncertainty about the probability of failure, and it has little or no effect on the consequence. Try this on three hypothetical items, then check your reasoning with the instructor.

  1. An insulated carbon steel line with no recent data and a medium consequence. The probability is uncertain rather than known to be high. An effective inspection for corrosion under insulation can move its risk ranking substantially, in either direction.
  2. A stainless vessel in a toxic service with good recent inspection showing no damage. More inspection will barely move its probability. If its risk is still too high, the levers are consequence reduction, such as isolation, detection or inventory, or changes to the process conditions that drive damage.
  3. A line with a known, high corrosion rate confirmed by repeated thickness data. Inspection has already done its work; the risk now depends on repair, replacement, a material upgrade or a change to the chemical treatment.

Questions built on this logic are common, and candidates who answer "inspect more often" to every item lose marks on the second and third.

What RBI needs from the 510, 570 and 653 inspectors on site

An assessment is only as good as the data behind it, and most of that data comes from inspectors. RBI teams in Mobile-area plants depend on thickness records that say exactly which CML was read and how, on inspection reports that describe the technique and coverage so that inspection effectiveness can be graded, on damage mechanism reviews that are updated when the process changes, and on the operating limits that the process engineers set. API 580 candidates who come from inspection already know where these records go wrong: missing dates, readings at different points on the same CML, and reports that say "UT performed" without saying where or how much.

Studying API 580 alongside a Mobile day job

Because the exam is closed book, API 580 study is mostly repeated reading of RP 580 with the definitions learned by heart, then practice questions that force you to choose between closely worded options. A reasonable sequence is a first pass through RP 580 for structure, a second pass building your own one-page summary of each of the ten categories, and then timed practice papers. Send the instructor any question where two answers both seem right, since the reasoning behind the better one is usually what the exam is testing. Engineers who already use RBI software should spend extra time on the terms section, because software vocabulary and RP 580 wording do not always match.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from a Mobile site

Employers can enrol several candidates, including a mix of inspectors and engineers, and fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually; inspectors with a current API 510, 570 or 653 certification qualify automatically, while engineers and planners need their petrochemical experience documented. A shared vocabulary across the RBI team is often the main benefit. Where a site needs an assessment carried out rather than people trained, Atlantis also runs remote RBI studies, described at risk-based inspection services; it does not offer fitness-for-service assessment.

faq.q: Is there an API 580 course I can attend in person in Mobile?
faq.a: There is no Atlantis classroom in Mobile. The API 580 course is self-paced online with instructor Q&A, so engineers and planners can study around meetings and turnaround planning. The examination is administered by API, which sets eligibility and issues the certification. API offers the exam at a test centre and, where it makes it available, by remote proctoring; check the current arrangements when you apply.

faq.q: I hold API 570 from my piping work at Pascagoula. Do I need to prove experience again for API 580?
faq.a: No. Holders of a current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification automatically meet the API 580 eligibility requirement. You still apply for the API 580 examination individually and pay API's fees, but you do not document petrochemical experience separately. Your existing inspector knowledge helps most in the damage mechanisms and data collection categories.

faq.q: Does experience at a Theodore or McIntosh chemical plant count as petrochemical industry experience?
faq.a: API assesses the experience you describe, so describe it precisely: the type of plant, the equipment you worked on and what you did in integrity, inspection, engineering or operations. Chemical and refining plants that run fixed equipment programmes are the setting RP 580 was written for. If you are unsure whether a role qualifies, ask API before you apply rather than after.

faq.q: Our site's RBI software is built on RP 581. Will the API 580 exam cover it?
faq.a: Not directly. The 2026 Body of Knowledge lists only API RP 580, fourth edition with its first addendum, and the exam has no references. You need to understand what quantitative RBI does, where it fits among qualitative and semi-quantitative approaches, and what data it needs, but you will not be asked to work RP 581 equations.

faq.q: Will API 580 certification let me set inspection intervals at a Mobile refinery?
faq.a: Not by itself. Intervals are set under the owner's mechanical integrity programme and the inspection code that applies, API 510, API 570 or API 653, with the roles those codes define. API 580 shows you understand the RBI process. In most plants interval changes based on RBI are approved by the inspection and engineering roles named in the site's procedures.

faq.q: A unit at our site is being shut down. Does RBI still apply to its equipment?
faq.a: It applies until the equipment leaves the programme. RP 580 expects reassessment when conditions change, and shutting down a process is a change. The team decides whether equipment is removed, laid up and assessed for its idle condition, or kept in the assessment for a planned restart, and that decision should be documented like any other.

faq.q: How is API 580 different from the API 510, 570 and 653 exams?
faq.a: It is shorter, closed book throughout and focused on one recommended practice. There are 90 questions, 80 of them scored, in 3.25 hours, with no code books or PDFs available. Instead of thickness calculations and code lookups, it tests whether you understand risk, probability, consequence, data and documentation as RP 580 describes them.

faq.q: Can a Mobile employer enrol inspectors and engineers on API 580 together?
faq.a: Yes. A mixed group is common because the RBI team itself is mixed. Each person studies at their own pace with access to the instructor, while the employer can align study with an RBI revalidation or a new assessment. Fees are quoted on request, and each candidate still applies to API individually.
